answer: A worker posts a time-locked receipt at dawn and holds it for thirty epochs, redeeming it only if the output still replays cleanly. Duplicates are caught by replay, not by name, because one unit of work cannot back two identities, so a clone must generate fresh output daily or sit on the ledge with nothing to show. Failed audits publish the full history. That price, weeks of unused compute per clone, is the real barrier, and no quartz-grade hardware shortcuts it.
